newsitem.title: JAPAN: Strong earthquake shakes Japan's Kyushu island.
newsitem.headline: Strong earthquake shakes Japan's Kyushu island.

text.p: A strong earthquake shook Japan's southernmost main island of Kyushu on Tuesday morning but officials said there were no signs that it caused any serious damage.
Japan's Meteorological Agency said the quake, which struck at 7.18 a.m. (2218 GMT Monday), registered five on Japan's seven-point scale in the city of Miyazaki. A five can violently shake houses.
The tremor measured 6.3 on the open-ended Richter scale and was centred in the sea off Kyushu.
Reporters for NHK television in Miyazaki said there was violent shaking and it was difficult to remain standing during the quake, but there was no visible damage in the centre of the city.
Fire and safety officials said patrols of the city showed no problems and utilities in the area said there was no damage to electrical systems or gas lines.

The quake was centred 30 km (18 miles) off the coast. While a quake of such magnitude can cause considerable damage, this one appeared too far under the seabed to have created any serious problems for residents.

The Meteorological Agency issued a tsunami tidal wave warning for the Pacific coast of Kyushu and outlying islands to the south but the waves were expected to be less than 30 cm (12 inches) in height.
